rationale: Tier B because this is a focused Java/Spring Boot backend for storing and retrieving healing results for Playwright/WebDriver tests, with moderate source depth (66 source files, 38 directories), one test class with 3 test methods using TestContainers, and no architecture or design documents. It provides selector persistence with scoring, a REST API to save/fetch healing attempts, and an optional AWS metrics pipeline. The core selector-matching intelligence (DOM tree comparison) is delegated to an external dependency (com.epam.healenium:tree-comparing:0.4.14), not implemented in this repo. The repo is specifically a storage backend for the larger Healenium ecosystem (healenium-client, hlm-selector-imitator), not a standalone healing algorithm. Licensed under Apache 2.0. Relevance to a Veridian scraping pipeline (self-healing concern) is moderate: the persistence layer design for selector healing outcomes and scoring could inform a self-healing sub-system, but the actual selector-fixing logic lives elsewhere. Score 6.5 reduced from potential 8 due to being only the backend storage half of a larger healing system.
limitations: Tree-comparing (DOM diffing for selector healing) is delegated to external Maven dependency com.epam.healenium:tree-comparing:0.4.14; no local source for the actual healing algorithm
Only 1 test file with 3 test methods; coverage is minimal
No architecture or design documents exist in the repository
Heavily coupled to Spring Boot 3.3 / JPA / PostgreSQL; not usable as a standalone library outside that stack
The README references a backend architecture diagram but the referenced image path is broken (uses local Downloads path)
Scrapes no data and contains no Playwright integration directly; it's a REST API that Playwright/WebDriver clients call to store/fetch healing results
GitLab CI and GitHub CI both present but CI content not deeply reviewed beyond presence
